items.title: Section: Four Ways Things Pair Off, Closing the Third Sutra

items.zh: 言相對者，謂有此故施設於彼，是名相對。此中諸受展轉相對，由彼一切苦所攝故。又由有此第一義苦，施設無智。由有此故，施設治彼出世之慧。由有此故，施設彼果寂滅涅槃。是故彼彼諸法，說與彼彼諸法相對。
items.en: Pairing means that because this exists, that is established in relation to it. Among these, the various feelings pair with one another, all being included within suffering. Because this ultimate suffering exists, ignorance is established in relation to it. Because this exists, the transcendent wisdom that overcomes it is established. Because this exists, its fruit, the cessation of nirvana, is established. Thus each of these phenomena is said to pair with each of the others.

items.title: Section: Ten Ways to Chase Off Sleep, and Five Ways to Keep What Concentration Is Won

items.zh: 謂勤修習內心寂靜奢摩他行諸苾芻等，為欲斷除諸隨煩惱，應知五種對治之相。謂遠離闇相；於能隨順舉歡喜法，發生正舉加行道理；損害諸見；諸見功用；諸見所依功用。
items.en: Monks earnestly cultivating the inner stillness of calm-abiding should know five antidotes for cutting off the secondary afflictions: removing the sign of darkness; rousing the mind through joyful reflection, giving rise to the principle of properly uplifting effort; damaging wrong views; damaging their function; and damaging their basis.

items.title: Section: Five Ways to Hold On to Concentration Once It Is Won

items.zh: 彼隨煩惱既斷滅已，復有五種任持定法。何等為五？謂諸遠離遠離處所、順定言說；順無染心資生眾具；從有智者同梵行所，獲得隨順教授教誡美妙言說；於諸世間等持、等至遠離愛味，及無漏行如理作意。
items.en: Once these secondary afflictions have been cut off, there are five further methods for sustaining concentration. What are the five? Solitude in every form; dwelling in a remote place while hearing teachings that accord with concentration; requisites of life giving rise to no defiled mind; receiving instruction and admonition in beautiful language from a wise fellow practitioner of pure conduct; and freeing the mind of craving towards worldly stabilising and culminating absorption while bringing correct attention to uncontaminated practice.

items.zh: 復次，彼勤修習增上心學諸苾芻等，由三因緣，當遣現行染污尋思。謂遠離所緣故。厭患自性故、遠離自性故。由三因緣，遠離自性。謂有對治力，根猛利者，能頓遠離。無對治力，根處中者，如其麁相能漸遠離。無對治力，根下劣者，於諸尋思因緣財食深見過患。復次，諸苾芻有六順出離界三摩地修習支者，謂諸苾芻於閑靜室勤修觀行，當知三種補特伽羅，有三三摩地。

items.title: Section: Three Persons, Three Immeasurables, and the Three Liberation Gates They Open

items.zh: 謂勤修習增上心者，於四有情怨行、惡行、淨行、恩行，有眾生緣定。又勤修習趣究竟者，有法緣定。又勤修習諦現觀者，有法緣定。
items.en: One earnestly cultivating the higher training in mind has concentration focused on beings, towards the four kinds of beings, those bearing enmity, those of unwholesome conduct, those of pure conduct, and benefactors. One earnestly cultivating progress towards the ultimate has concentration focused on phenomena. One earnestly cultivating direct realisation of the truths has concentration with no object of reference at all.

items.title: Section: Three Kinds of Greatness, Two Kinds of Solitude, and Fascicle Sixty-Two's Own Close

items.zh: 復次，由三種大性大三摩地，能令速疾通達真如；既通達已，能盡諸漏。謂由所緣大性故，由精勤大性故，由方便所攝作意大性故。又有二遠離，能令速疾通達真如。謂於行處遠離憒閙，及於住處離惡尋思。
items.en: Furthermore, three kinds of greatness produce the great concentration able to swiftly penetrate suchness. Once suchness is penetrated, every outflow can be exhausted. These are greatness of object, greatness of diligence, and greatness of the skilfully embraced attention. There are also two kinds of solitude able to swiftly penetrate suchness: solitude from rowdiness in ordinary activity, and freedom from unwholesome deliberation while dwelling in practice.

blocks.text: Practical advice: how to stay awake in meditation, how to keep what concentration you have won, and the three levels of immeasurable love.
Master Cháng Bǎi: because this exists, that is designated: wisdom is the antidote, ignorance what it overcomes.
Master Cháng Bǎi: leave the dark state, using the perception of light. When the mind sinks, attend to bright, joyful objects: the Buddha, Dharma, Saṅgha, giving, precepts.

Master Cháng Bǎi: use requisites that do not stir clinging, so one need not keep going out for them. Do not stop at worldly concentration; go on to undefiled contemplation. (Untranslated, 0648a14: three ways to dispel defiled thoughts: keep away from their object, see their nature as faulty, and leave them; the sharp do it at once, the middling gradually, the dull by seeing the faults of the gain and food that cause them.)

Master Cháng Bǎi: first the practitioner still senses individual beings; towards enemies, wish them happiness; towards benefactors, wish them free of greed. Then, seeing beings as only conditioned aggregates, one cultivates the immeasurables on phenomena alone; finally without any object.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the place of activity is ordinary life; the place of dwelling is the time of calm and insight. Diligence is the greatness that matters most.
The Stage of Concentration ascertained: the obstacles (mostly honesty), the attainments, and the warning not to cling even to meditation's joys.

quiz.q: What does "pairing" mean, and what kind of pairing are wisdom with ignorance, and path with cessation?
options: pairing means enmity, all things opposing each other, as the lecture says
pairing means sameness
pairing means order in time
because this exists that is set up; wisdom and ignorance are antidote and overcome, path and cessation cause and fruit
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: because this exists, that is designated. Transcendent wisdom is the antidote and ignorance what is overcome; wisdom as the path is the cause, and the fruit designated from it is cessation. The word covers more than one relation.

quiz.q: Monks cultivating calm-abiding should know five antidotes. Which is among them?
options: leaving villages and dwelling alone in the wilderness, the first condition for meditation
taking the one-day restraint
reciting the sutras
removing the sign of darkness
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: removing the sign of darkness means leaving the dark state so as not to feel sleepy, which is treated by the perception of light. The English lacks the heading of the sutra, so this list may seem to continue the previous one.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain rousing the mind through joyful reflection?
options: when dull, one reflects on joyful things such as the Jewels, giving, and precepts, and so uplifts the mind
when restless, one reflects on impermanence and suffering to calm down, 舉 being restlessness
one cultivates loving-kindness against anger
one gets up to walk around a Buddha image
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: when the mind sinks or sleep threatens, one attends to pure, fine objects, joyful things such as the Buddha, Dharma, Sangha, giving, precepts, and the gods, and rouses the mind. Here 舉 is uplifting, not restlessness.

quiz.q: What does Master Cháng Bǎi say damaging views, their function, and their basis refer to?
options: cutting greed, hatred, and delusion in turn, as the roots of all views
cutting broken precepts, views, and deportment
cutting wrong views, the wrong conduct they produce, and the self-grasping they rest on
cutting views of the three realms in turn
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the third cuts wrong views; the fourth cuts the wrong conduct they produce, such as cow and dog observances; the fifth cuts the self-grasping on which they rest, since all wrong thought comes from it.

quiz.q: Among the five ways of sustaining concentration, what is said of requisites of life?
options: requisites of life giving rise to no defiled mind
the more abundant the better, so one should seek the finest food and bedding
using no requisites at all
only those offered by donors
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: use requisites that do not give rise to a clinging mind; then one need not keep going out to seek them and has time for meditation. So modest supply serves concentration, neither luxury nor total denial.

quiz.q: In the last of the five, what is the attitude towards worldly concentration?
options: freeing the mind of craving for it, and bringing correct attention to undefiled practice
resting in it fully with no need for more, it being the final achievement
abandoning worldly concentration altogether
practising it only at the time of death
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: do not stop at the stage of worldly concentration; relying on what is gained, go on to undefiled contemplation such as the four truths and attain undefiled concentration joined with transcendent wisdom. Worldly concentration remains the base.

quiz.q: What concentration has each: the one on the higher mind, on the ultimate, and on realisation of the truths?
options: no object, then beings, then phenomena, the higher mind going deepest, as the text orders them
all three focused on phenomena
all three with no object
concentration focused on beings, focused on phenomena, and with no object
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the practitioner still senses individual beings, and cultivates the immeasurable states with the idea of beings. Then come phenomena, and finally no object. The English lacks the heading that presents these as three persons.

quiz.q: What does Master Cháng Bǎi say one cultivates towards the hostile and the kind? (This is the lecture's assignment.)
options: towards the hostile, equanimity, as they deserve no attention; towards benefactors, love, as repayment
towards the hostile, wishing them happiness, loving-kindness; towards benefactors, wishing them to let go of afflictions, equanimity
compassion towards the hostile, joy towards the kind
joy towards the hostile, compassion towards the kind
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: towards those who bear enmity, wish them happiness and cultivate loving-kindness; towards benefactors, wish them to give up greed, hatred, and delusion, and cultivate equanimity. The treatise only lists the four kinds of beings.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain concentration focused on phenomena and with no object?
options: the first is reciting texts, and the second is thinking of nothing at all
the first focuses on the Buddha, the second on the Sangha
the first sees beings as mere aggregates with no being to find; the second sees phenomena themselves as unfindable
the first focuses on precepts, the second on the gods
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: seeing that these beings are only aggregates born of conditions, with no being to be found, one cultivates the immeasurables on phenomena alone. Seeing that the aggregates too cannot be found, and leaving discrimination, one enters undefiled wisdom.

quiz.q: What are the three greatnesses of the great concentration that swiftly penetrates suchness?
options: greatness of merit, of wisdom, and of miraculous power
greatness of body, speech, and mind
greatness of precepts, meditation, and wisdom
greatness of object, of diligence, and of the skilfully embraced attention
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: through the method of the three greatnesses, great concentration quickly penetrates the suchness of reality; greatness of diligence is especially strong effort. Several readings of each exist, so only the names are tested.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain the "place of activity" and "place of dwelling" in the two kinds of solitude?
options: activity is one's walking path and dwelling one's room, purely outer arrangements
activity is daily life, away from rowdiness; dwelling is the time of calm and insight, free of unwholesome thoughts
activity is alms round, dwelling is sleep
activity is teaching, dwelling is listening
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the place of activity means ordinary life outside practice, away from noise and mixing with others. The place of dwelling means the time of calm and insight, free of unwholesome thoughts such as desire and ill will. Body and mind are both covered.
